title: The Lion-man

source.author: Dagmar Hollmann
source.notes: Original figurine photographed in Museum Ulm, frontal three-quarter view on a plain dark background; this is also the English Wikipedia infobox image. File metadata from the Commons imageinfo API. Object data: Dates: Wikipedia (35,000-41,000 years old; Wikidata inception c. 38,000 BCE). Dimensions 31.1 x 5.6 x 5.9 cm: Wikipedia lead. Find-spot coordinates: Wikidata Q1498134 (Hohlenstein-Stadel). Discovery date: Wikipedia/Wikidata. Museum Ulm inventory number not published on Wikipedia/Wikidata.

object.description: A standing figure with a human body and the head of a cave lion, carved from a mammoth tusk with flint tools. Found in fragments in the Hohlenstein-Stadel cave in the Swabian Jura in 1939, it was reassembled over decades from more than two hundred pieces and is among the oldest known figurative sculptures.
facts: Discovered on 25 August 1939 by Otto Völzing, a week before the Second World War halted the dig.
Radiocarbon dating of its find layer places it between 35,000 and 41,000 years old.
Seven parallel transverse gouges are carved into the left arm; the 2012-13 restoration raised its height from 29.6 to 31.1 cm.

tour: The Lion-man, carved from mammoth ivory 40,000 years ago: a creature no one had ever seen. The oldest image of something imagined.
